anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Excessive or uncontrolled engine memory growth pushes the database process and host beyond the safe physical-memory envelope, triggering paging, OOM kills, or node eviction.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions serialize on buffer-cache pages and their latches, spending time on buffer-busy or page-latch waits instead of useful work.

When both anomalies strike together, the system exhibits a mixed memory-pressure / latch-pressure profile: resident-set size climbs steadily while CPU cores oscillate between spinning on latches and stalling in OS scheduler queues. Wait-event dashboards show simultaneous memory-pressure stalls, page-in/page-out spikes, and elevated BUFFER_BUSY or PAGE_LATCH waits. Throughput collapses irregularly, with latency outliers tied to hot pages whose eviction, re-allocation, or dirty-page flushing is repeatedly blocked. Checkpoints stretch out, background writers fall behind, and sessions experience cascading slowdowns or abrupt terminations as the OS begins to reclaim memory.

Causal chain: Unbounded memory allocation inflates the buffer pool and related work areas; when physical RAM is exhausted, the OS starts paging, shrinking the effective cache and forcing constant page churn. This churn raises the probability that many sessions request the same few reloaded pages, aggravating latch contention. Conversely, heavy latch contention lengthens the residency of hot pages and defers their flush or eviction, which keeps them—and their metadata—pinned in memory, accelerating memory consumption. Each condition therefore amplifies the other: memory pressure induces hotter pages and more latch fights, while latch fights prolong page lifetimes and inflate memory, jointly pushing the database toward severe instability, throughput collapse, and potential crashes.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time after which a TCP keepalive message that has not been acknowledged by the client should be retransmitted.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP keepalive probe is not acknowledged for tcp_keepalives_interval on systems supporting TCP_KEEPINTVL or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Controls retry timing for keepalive probes used to detect unresponsive client connections.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
